claims: The Michigan "Fab Five" refers to the 1991 University of Michigan men's basketball recruiting class—Chris Webber, Jalen Rose, Juwan Howard, Jimmy King, and Ray Jackson.
The Fab Five were the first all-freshman starting lineup to reach the NCAA title game.
The Fab Five reached consecutive national championship games in 1992 and 1993.
The Fab Five members are Chris Webber (#4), Jalen Rose (#5), Juwan Howard (#25), Jimmy King (#24), and Ray Jackson (#21).
The Fab Five popularized baggy shorts.
The Fab Five popularized black socks.
The Fab Five brought a "street" style of play and swagger to the college game.
The Fab Five played in the 1992 NCAA championship game, losing to Duke.
The Fab Five played in the 1993 NCAA championship game, losing to North Carolina.
A scandal involving improper payments resulted in the University of Michigan disassociating from certain Fab Five members.
A scandal involving improper payments resulted in the University of Michigan removing their banners.
The Fab Five members reunited for an alternative broadcast during the 2026 Final Four.
Four of the five Fab Five members (Webber, Rose, Howard, King) played in the NBA.
Juwan Howard won two NBA championships.
